# Photoshop Lab ASE fixture

`photoshop-lab.ase` is an unmodified copy of Ger Hobbelt's
`LAB.colorspace.test.ase` from the Photoshop-to-D3 ASE loader demonstration:

- Project: https://gist.github.com/GerHobbelt/3173233
- Pinned binary: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/GerHobbelt/3173233/raw/174c53a72310870b5e80051ba587f04a84cfb721/LAB.colorspace.test.ase
- Gist revision: `1258b57b50cfeef4aee71624d1780b000a5852e0`
- SHA-256: `8d3e9572838755bdb84d171da7eb592572d9e5a465687151c6edec2b126f5405`

The demonstration describes the Photoshop “Save Swatches for Exchange” workflow;
its loader explicitly identifies Photoshop CS5.5 as storing Lab lightness in
0–1. This is a published external fixture, not an ASE generated by our tests.
The author supplies the provenance; we have not re-exported it in Adobe software.
The file contains one CMYK swatch and these three Lab swatches:

| Name | Stored L | a* | b* | Reference sRGB bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| LAB 1 | 0.88238525390625 | -47 | 9 | 108, 245, 202 |
| LAB 2 | 0.88238525390625 | 117 | 120 | 255, 39, 0 |
| Swatch 1 | 0.5216064453125 | 77 | -16 | 229, 29, 155 |

Reference values were calculated independently of Core Graphics using CIELAB
lightness `100 * stored L`, D50 white `(0.96422, 1, 0.82521)`, the CIE Lab-to-XYZ
inverse, Bradford D50-to-D65 adaptation, the XYZ-to-linear-sRGB matrix, and the
sRGB transfer function. Clamp final sRGB components to 0–1 and round to bytes.
These operations and matrices are documented in the W3C CSS Color 4 sample
conversion code: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#color-conversion-code
The references test conversion mathematics, not Photoshop's rendering intent
or a comparison with Adobe-exported RGB values. Tests allow one byte for
ColorSync rounding differences.

Core Graphics' default Lab range produces approximately `(30, 251, 197)`,
`(255, 0, 0)`, and `(254, 0, 163)` for these swatches. The explicit symmetric
`[-127.5, 127.5]` range gives standard CIELAB scaling; using `[-128, 127]`
introduces an offset even for neutral gray. WebKit documents the same Core
Graphics requirement here:
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=220684#c18

CMYK output is deliberately not assigned fixed reference bytes: ASE embeds no
CMYK profile, and the importer uses the system's device CMYK conversion.
